text: If I had more time, I'd learn to play the harp.
tip: 'I'd' is a short /aɪd/. Stress TIME and HARP. Pause a little at the comma.

text: I've been living here for nearly three years.
tip: 'I've been' squeezes into /aɪv bɪn/ because 'been' is weak. Stress LIV-ing, NEAR-ly and THREE.

text: The bridge was built by the villagers a hundred years ago.
tip: 'was' is weak /wəz/. 'built' rhymes with 'kilt' because the 'u' is silent.

text: She asked me whether I'd ever been to Scotland.
tip: 'asked' is /ɑːskt/, which is tricky! In fast speech many people say /ɑːst/. Stress SCOT-land.

text: You should have told me you were coming.
tip: 'should have' sounds like /ˈʃʊdəv/. Never write 'should of'!

text: Although it was raining, we decided to go for a walk.
tip: 'decided' has /ɪd/: de-CI-ded. Pause briefly after 'raining'.

text: I'm used to getting up early because of my job.
tip: 'used to' has an /s/, not a /z/: /ˈjuːstə/. Link 'getting up' into 'gettin-gup'.

text: The museum, which is in the city centre, is free on Sundays.
tip: Pause at both commas because the 'which' clause is extra information. Stress mu-SE-um.

text: I'm thinking of applying for a job at the bookshop.
tip: ap-PLY-ing has the stress in the middle. Link 'thinking of' into 'thinkin-gof'.

text: We'd better hurry, or we'll miss the last train.
tip: Keep the end sound: 'we'd' /wiːd/ and 'we'll' /wiːl/ must sound different.

text: Have you ever tried the cheese they make in this valley?
tip: Yes/no questions usually rise at the end. Keep /tr/ together in 'tried' /traɪd/.

text: It's the most interesting story I've ever read.
tip: 'interesting' often has three syllables: /ˈɪntrəstɪŋ/. Here 'read' is past, so say /red/.

text: Unless the weather improves, the festival will be cancelled.
tip: 'improves' ends in /vz/. 'cancelled' is /ˈkænsld/ with two syllables.

text: I'd rather stay at home than go to the crowded market.
tip: 'rather' and 'than' both have a buzzy /ð/. 'crowded' ends in /ɪd/.

text: The owl, who had been asleep all day, suddenly opened its eyes.
tip: Say it in three chunks: The owl | who had been asleep all day | suddenly opened its eyes.

text: Could you tell me what time the next boat leaves?
tip: Indirect questions often fall at the end. In 'next boat', say just one /t/: /neks bəʊt/.

text: My grandmother used to tell us stories about the old castle.
tip: Stress GRAND-mother, STOR-ies and CAS-tle. 'used to' is /ˈjuːstə/.

text: Neither my brother nor I could find the way home.
tip: British 'neither' is usually /ˈnaɪðə/. Stress BROTH-er and I.

q: Describe your perfect weekend. Use 'would' and 'because'.
model: My perfect weekend would start with a long walk because I love being outside.
tip: Make it one smooth sentence. 'would' is often weak /wəd/, or you can say 'it'd'.

q: Tell me about something you have never done. Start with 'I've never…'.
model: I've never been to Japan, but I would love to go one day.
tip: 'I've never' links into /aɪv ˈnevə/. Stress NEV-er and the place.

q: Give some advice to a friend who always feels tired. Use 'should'.
model: You should go to bed earlier and drink more water during the day.
tip: 'should' is weak /ʃəd/. Stress the advice itself: BED, EAR-li-er, WA-ter.

q: What will you do if it rains tomorrow? Begin with 'If it rains'.
model: If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay at home and read a good book.
tip: 'I'll' counts as 'I will'. Pause after the 'if' part and stress the main verb.
